title: So pretexto de: una justificación oficial cuestionable

sections.content: So pretexto de (under the pretext of) introduces an official justification the writer is signaling as doubtful -- distinct from a neutral connector, it carries built-in skepticism about whether the stated reason was the real one. Exactly the tool for describing Cold War interventions whose declared goals rarely matched their actual motives. These sentences are taken directly from the previous reading.

items.spanish: La CIA organizó un golpe de Estado contra Árbenz, so pretexto de que su reforma agraria representaba una amenaza comunista para la región.
items.english: The CIA organized a coup against Árbenz, under the pretext that his land reform represented a communist threat to the region.

items.spanish: So pretexto de restaurar el orden constitucional, Estados Unidos envió más de veinte mil soldados a la República Dominicana.
items.english: Under the pretext of restoring constitutional order, the United States sent more than twenty thousand soldiers to the Dominican Republic.

items.spanish: So pretexto de apoyar la autodeterminación de los pueblos, la URSS y Cuba proporcionaron entrenamiento militar a movimientos guerrilleros.
items.english: Under the pretext of supporting peoples' self-determination, the USSR and Cuba provided military training to guerrilla movements.

items.spanish: Este patrón de intervención, justificada so pretexto de principios elevados, estaba motivado con frecuencia por cálculos mucho más pragmáticos.
items.english: This pattern of intervention, justified under the pretext of lofty principles, was frequently motivated by far more pragmatic calculations.

sections.content: So pretexto de is somewhat archaic and formal -- you'll mostly meet it in historical or legal writing, where it works exactly like bajo el pretexto de but in a more compact, literary register.
